practiceReport.name: Drake Maye
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (88% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: The timetable put forth by Rapoport suggests that Maye could make a run at a late-season return, or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Given that the Patriots are already close to the limit of how many players they can designate for return from injured reserve, Maye isn't a lock to land on IR, but he's nonetheless facing an absence longer than the required four games that a placement on IR would mandate. For now, Tommy DeVito has been installed as the team's starter ahead of its Week 12 matchup against the Chargers, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup.

practiceReport.name: A.J. Brown
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: New England's trade for Brown is going down as one the team would definitely prefer to reverse. He's shown no chemistry with Drake Maye (ankle) and hasn't looked healthy since injuring his ankle in the first half of the Week 1 game against the Seahawks. Brown also appears to have lost multiple steps with his downfield speed due to the laundry list of lower-body injuries that now includes ankle, knee and hamstring issues in 2026. The Patriots will play out the string on a lost season without Maye and Brown for several more weeks. Look for Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) when healthy, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism to pick up the slack at wideout with Brown on the shelf again.

practiceReport.name: Greg Van Roten
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (G) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Van Roten will be available to make his season debut after spending the first nine weeks of the campaign on injured reserve due to the hamstring issue. He was able to practice throughout Week 10 prep, turning in a pair of a limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full activity Friday, and the Patriots activated him Saturday. With Ben Brown (knee) and Walter Rouse (concussion) inactive for the Germany game, Van Roten will likely draw the start at left guard.
